title: What Percentage Is a 7 in IB? Grade Guide
summary: What percentage is a 7 in IB? Learn why boundaries change by subject, session and level, with dated examples and a reliable way to check your weighted score.
body_markdown:
**What percentage is a 7 in IB?** There is no single percentage that always earns a 7. The minimum mark changes by subject, Standard Level or Higher Level, examination session and, where applicable, time zone. In recent subjects, a 7 has sometimes begun in the low 70s, while other boundaries have been closer to 80%.


The reliable answer is the published boundary for your exact course and session.


Imagine a student seeing 74% on a marked Mathematics paper. Is that a 7 or a 6? The percentage alone cannot answer. The relevant IB grade boundary gives it meaning.


### The short answer at a glance


Before interpreting an IB percentage, check five details:


- The full subject name
- Standard Level or Higher Level
- The assessment session, such as May 2025
- The applicable time zone or examination variant
- Whether the mark represents one component or the final weighted subject score


RevisionDojo's[IB Grade Boundaries tool](https://www.revisiondojo.com/grade-boundaries) shows historical boundaries and the minimum scores associated with each grade.


A parent aims an oversized calculator at a report card while a student explains that they need the correct boundary first


### Why a 7 does not have one fixed percentage


IB subject grades run from 1 to 7, with 7 representing the highest achievement level. The scale is not a permanent percentage conversion chart.


Assessments may include written examinations, oral work, practical work or internal assessment. Each component carries a weighting. Component marks are scaled and combined into a final percentage total before the subject grade is assigned.


For illustration, if examinations contributed 80% and internal assessment contributed 20%, examination performance of 75% and internal assessment performance of 70% would produce 74% overall. Actual structures and weightings vary by course.


The International Baccalaureate uses professional judgment, statistical evidence and grade descriptors when establishing boundaries. This helps maintain comparable standards when assessments differ in difficulty. It does not mean a fixed proportion of students must receive each grade.


RevisionDojo's guide to[how IB grade boundaries are calculated](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-grade-boundaries-how-theyre-actually-calculated) explores that distinction.


### Dated examples of IB grade boundaries


Consider these published RevisionDojo examples for May 2025:


May 2025 course example Reported final grade 7 range


Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL 79-100


Digital Society HL 72-100


Global Politics HL 72-100


A 75% final weighted score would sit inside the illustrated grade 7 range for Digital Society HL and Global Politics HL, but below the illustrated Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL threshold.


Confirm the exact session and variant attached to your results. The[Mathematics AA HL 2025 boundary guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-mathematics-analysis-and-approaches-hl-2025-grade-boundaries-guide) demonstrates why individual courses need separate consideration.


Historical numbers are reference points, not promises. RevisionDojo's overview of[IB grade boundaries by year](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-grade-boundaries-by-year-what-a-7-requires) illustrates how thresholds can move between sessions and, sometimes, time zones.


### How to convert your percentage into an IB grade


The hypothetical student with 74% can follow a straightforward checking process.


### Confirm what the percentage represents


A score on one paper is not automatically the final subject percentage. It must be combined with the other components using their correct weightings.


For example, 74% on an examination and 68% on an internal assessment do not necessarily average to 71%. That calculation works only if those components contribute equally.


### Select the exact course and session


Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches is not interchangeable with Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation. HL boundaries should not be applied to SL work, and one subject's thresholds cannot be transferred to another.


Likewise, a May 2024 boundary provides historical context for a May 2025 student, not the definitive conversion. RevisionDojo's[guide to understanding IB grade boundaries](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/understanding-ib-grade-boundaries-2025-what-they-mean-and-how-to-use-them) explains these labels.


### Compare the weighted total with the lower boundary


If the relevant grade 7 boundary is 72, a final weighted score of 72 reaches that threshold. A score of 71 falls into the next grade band.


One mark can therefore change the reported grade. That threshold is an assessment decision, not a judgment about the student's intelligence or potential.


### What predicted IB grades actually mean


Schools may use practice assessments, coursework and teacher judgment to estimate grades, sometimes applying historical boundaries to percentages.


These predictions are useful but provisional. The eventual boundary can differ from the benchmark used during the year. School assessments may also differ from official assessments in difficulty, weighting or marking approach.


Read a predicted 6 or 7 as an estimate of current performance under the school's chosen approach. RevisionDojo's[IB grade boundaries explained guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-grade-boundaries-explained) offers additional context for interpreting these estimates.


### Set a target with room for uncertainty


When planning revision, use the historical threshold as a starting point and aim above it. There is no universal buffer that guarantees a 7. Your target should reflect how consistent your performance is across topics and under timed conditions.


Suppose a relevant historical boundary is 72% and your last three comparable practice scores are 69%, 74% and 73%. You have reached that benchmark twice, but the variation suggests that a 7 is not yet secure. Review the lost marks across all three attempts. Repeated errors deserve more attention than an isolated mistake on an unfamiliar question.


Keep a simple record of the score, component, conditions and main errors for each attempt. This makes your progress easier to interpret and gives your teacher something concrete to discuss when recommending the next revision priority.


### Use boundaries to choose your next study step


If you sit four marks below a historical 7 threshold, identify where those marks could come from. Are command terms being misread? Do explanations lack subject vocabulary? Is working missing from otherwise correct calculations?

Parents can use the same approach: ask what was assessed, how it was weighted and which boundary was applied before interpreting a percentage.


So, what percentage is a 7 in IB? The answer belongs to a particular course, level and session. Check those details in RevisionDojo's[Grade Boundaries tool](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/grade-boundaries) , then turn the result into a practical study decision.
